Every tiny paper fibre lines up cleanly, like two halves of a broken teacup pieced together!
Read the cake baking recipe aloud, Mei, so I can copy it down nice and neatly.
Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yí bàn. Combines 一 ('one') + 半 ('half'); note yī shifts to yí before 4th-tone bàn.

examples.text: 这壶热茶我们已经喝了一半。
examples.trans: We have already drunk half of this pot of hot tea.

examples.text: 第二页乐谱有一半还没有写完。
examples.trans: Half of the second page of sheet music is still unfinished.

examples.text: 一百人。
examples.trans: One hundred people.

examples.text: 一百个。
examples.trans: One hundred.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yì qǐ. Placed right before the verb to mean 'together' (一起吃晚饭 'have dinner together').

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

examples.text: 等等，让我把平板屏幕和纸本子放一起看。
examples.trans: Wait—let me look at the tablet screen and the paper ledger side by side.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个下午 ('an afternoon').

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

examples.text: 先别对外面透露一个字！让两兄弟先过完这个星期五下午！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià lái. Compound directional complement for downward motion or writing something down to keep.

examples.text: 快问他叫什么名字！记下来！
examples.trans: Quick, ask him what his name is! Write it down!

examples.text: 请一定写下来！三楼热水：满分十分！
examples.trans: Please be sure to write that down! Third-floor hot water: ten out of ten!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià cì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 下一次 ('the next occasion').

examples.text: 下次来成都，一定再来住我们客栈！
examples.trans: Next time you come to Chengdu, be sure to stay at our inn again!

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，我们下次见！
examples.trans: It was lovely chatting today—see you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Standard negation for present/future/habitual verbs and adjectives; shifts to bú before a 4th tone (不是 bú shì).

examples.text: 停电的时候，纸还能用。
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Classifier after 一/半 for tiny amounts of hope, chance, or feeling.

examples.text: 只要还有一丝希望，我们就绝不放弃。
examples.trans: As long as a shred of hope remains, we will never give up.

examples.text: 他的语气里没有露出一丝紧张。
examples.trans: Not the slightest trace of nerves showed in his voice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng jiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 正中间 ('the exact middle').

examples.text: 当然不能偷看……咦，自己翻开在中间那页了！
examples.trans: Of course we must not peek... oh, it fell open to the middle page by itself!

examples.text: 两栋砖房中间是一个安静的小院。
examples.trans: Between the two brick buildings lies a quiet small courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a noun used in conversational Mandarin. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个书脊 ('a 书脊').

examples.text: 我有一个书脊。
examples.trans: I have a 书脊.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的书脊。
examples.trans: This is a very good 书脊.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mǎi. Everyday verb for purchasing goods; contrasts in tone with 卖 (mài 'sell').

examples.text: 看我的！快说要买什么。
examples.trans: Watch me! Tell me quickly what to buy.

examples.text: 九分钟！牛奶、鸡蛋和苹果都买来了！
examples.trans: Nine minutes! The milk, eggs, and apples are all here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ. Everyday singular 'you' among colleagues, friends, and peers; use 您 for polite respect.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàng. Introduces a likeness or example ('look like, be like').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 他长得真像他哥哥。
examples.trans: He really looks like his older brother.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chū lái. Directional complement for coming out or figuring something out (认出来).

examples.text: 明信片上整齐的方格字，我两秒钟就认出来了。
examples.trans: That neat block handwriting on the postcard—I recognized it in two seconds.

examples.text: 看合页边露出来的折纸图纸——一楼画着一扇暗门！
examples.trans: Look at the folded blueprint sticking out of the hinge—a hidden door is drawn on the ground floor!

related.gloss: come fresh out of the oven

meanings.note: Pinyin: fēn zhōng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 五分钟 ('five minutes').

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuā. Used for painting walls, brushing, or swiping a card.

examples.text: 一到七号钥匙全拿走了，八号房刚刷了油漆。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight just got fresh paint.

examples.text: 周末我们要刷院子里的木门。
examples.trans: This weekend we are going to paint the wooden courtyard gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo. Used both as a noun (勺子 'spoon') and as a measure word for spoonfuls (一勺蜂蜜 'a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 喝热柠檬茶的时候，加一勺蜂蜜最香。
examples.trans: Hot lemon tea smells best when you add a spoonful of honey.

examples.text: 请给我拿一把干净的小木勺。
examples.trans: Please bring me a clean little wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàn. Follows a measure word for 'and a half' (七点半 '7:30') or precedes a measure word for 'half a' (半个小时).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Small paper card for notes, gifts, or study.

examples.text: 礼物盒里放着一张小卡片。
examples.trans: Inside the gift box sits a small card.

examples.text: 他在卡片上写了几句祝福。
examples.trans: He wrote a few wishes on the card.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lì shǐ. Measure word (量词): 段, e.g. 一段历史 ('a stretch of history').

examples.text: 一位研究成都历史小院建筑的建筑师啊！
examples.trans: An architect who studies historic courtyard buildings in Chengdu!

examples.text: 这条老街已经有两百年的历史了。
examples.trans: This old street already has two hundred years of history.

related.gloss: a stretch of history (measure word 段)

压.gloss: press down; weigh down; pin underneath

meanings.en: press down; weigh down; pin underneath
meanings.note: Pinyin: yā. Action verb for pressing from above or holding flat under an object (压着 'pinned/resting underneath').

examples.text: 快看铁盒子最底下的薄纸下面，还压着一个小方信封！
examples.trans: Look underneath the tissue paper at the very bottom of the tin box—a tiny square envelope is tucked underneath!

examples.text: 老陈拿了一块光滑的鹅卵石，把桌上的图纸压稳。
examples.trans: Chen took a smooth river pebble to weight the drawing paper down steadily on the table.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chú fáng. Measure word (量词): 间 (jiān), e.g. 一间厨房 ('a kitchen').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 糟了！周经理，小晴，厨房出急事了！
examples.trans: Oh no! Manager Zhou, Qing, we have a kitchen emergency!

meanings.note: Pinyin: kě. Adds emphatic warmth before an adjective/verb, or means 'but'.

examples.text: 我可不穿四十四码的鞋！
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!

examples.text: 今天外面的风可真大。
examples.trans: The wind outside today is really strong.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Placed at the end of any statement to turn it into a neutral yes/no question.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: tīng. Focuses on the act of listening; add 见 or 到 (听见, 听到) for actually hearing.

examples.text: 老陈，你听到了吗？有人按了大门门铃！
examples.trans: Chen, did you hear that? Someone rang the front gate bell!

examples.text: 我在院子里老远就听到你们喊黄油了。
examples.trans: All the way out in the courtyard I heard you shouting about butter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Sentence-final particle reminding the listener of something natural or obvious.

examples.text: 总得有人照顾院子里的花草嘛。
examples.trans: Somebody has to look after the courtyard plants, after all.

examples.text: 都是老街坊，不用客气嘛。
examples.trans: We are all old neighbors—no need to be so formal.

examples.text: 这本厚厚的留言簿已经记录了四十位客人的故事。
examples.trans: This thick guestbook has already recorded the stories of forty guests.

examples.text: 这条老街上超过四十年的老字号店铺还有好几家。
examples.trans: There are still several time-honored shops over forty years old along this historic street.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yīn wèi. Introduces a reason; often paired with 所以 ('therefore') in the next clause.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 因为楼梯窄，而且周经理在那儿放了旧灯箱子。
examples.trans: Because the stairs are narrow, and Manager Zhou put old lamp boxes up there.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Neutral-tone structural particle turning a descriptive phrase into an adverb before a verb (轻轻地放 'set down gently'); distinct from noun di4 ('ground').

examples.text: 小晴整整齐齐地把茶杯排在木架上。
examples.trans: Qing arranged the teacups neatly on the wooden shelf.

examples.text: 老陈仔细地检查了每一根新电线。
examples.trans: Chen carefully checked every single new wire.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mò shuǐ. Liquid writing ink for fountain pens. Measure word: 瓶 (píng, 'bottle').

examples.text: 这页旧信是用深蓝色墨水写的。
examples.trans: This old letter page was written in dark blue ink.

examples.text: 桌上的钢笔没墨水了，我得去加一点。
examples.trans: The fountain pen on the desk is out of ink; I need to refill it.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà. Everyday adjective for size, age, and strong wind or rain.

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà shēng. Combines 大 ('big/loud') + 声 ('voice/sound'); modifies verbs of speaking or reading directly (大声念 'read aloud').

examples.text: 小晴，把木牌上的字大声念给我听听吧。
examples.trans: Qing, read the words on the wooden sign aloud for me to hear.

examples.text: 周经理在院子里大声宣布九号房咖啡角正式通过了审核。
examples.trans: In the courtyard, Manager Zhou announced aloud that the Room Nine café corner had officially passed the review.

太好了.gloss: wonderful!; that's great!; good thing too!

meanings.en: wonderful!; that's great!; good thing too!
meanings.note: Pinyin: tài hǎo le. Exclamatory frame 太...了 ('so / exceedingly...') around 好 ('good').

examples.text: 那太好了，大厨，我们刚从集市买回四十个新鲜柠檬。
examples.trans: That's wonderful, chef—we just brought back forty fresh lemons from the market.

examples.text: 太好了，雨终于停了，我们可以把折叠椅搬到院子里了！
examples.trans: Wonderful—the rain has finally stopped, so we can carry the folding chairs out into the courtyard!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiā. First-tone jiā: hold something pinched between two surfaces, such as under one's arm (夹在胳膊底下) or inside book pages.

examples.text: 周经理把绿色登记本夹在胳膊底下走来走去。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou paced back and forth with the green guest book tucked under his arm.

examples.text: 她在旧书里夹了一片干树叶做书签。
examples.trans: She tucked a dried leaf inside the old book as a bookmark.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular pronoun for objects, animals, and places.

examples.text: 是啊，宋老师，还在等它的主人呢。
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, still waiting for its owner.

examples.text: 别念叨它，宋老师！我现在差不多喜欢上那两声响了。
examples.trans: Don't tempt it, Teacher Song! I have almost grown fond of those two rings now.

meanings.note: Pinyin: duì. Means 'correct!' on its own, 'right' as a result complement (拿对), or 'to/toward' before a noun.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 看拉链旁边……对，有她的名字缩写！
examples.trans: Check beside the zipper... yes, her name initials are here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháng chang. Softened reduplication of 尝 ('taste'), standard when inviting someone to sample food.

examples.text: 快来尝尝我刚烤出来的杏仁柠檬挞！
examples.trans: Come have a taste of the almond lemon tart I just baked!

examples.text: 你先尝尝这碗番茄汤咸淡合适不合适。
examples.trans: Have a taste of this tomato soup first to see if the seasoning is right.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Highlights immediacy, exact location (就在这里), or smooth consequence ('then').

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a adv used in conversational Mandarin.

examples.text: 我有一个工工整整。
examples.trans: I have a 工工整整.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的工工整整。
examples.trans: This is a very good 工工整整.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gàn. Read gàn when meaning 'do work / get a job done' (干得不错 'nicely done!').

examples.text: 第二天上班，干得不错，新手。
examples.trans: For day two on the job, nicely done, rookie.

examples.text: 不许盯着客人看。把箱子交还，干自己的活。
examples.trans: No staring at guests. Hand back the bag and do our own work.

meanings.note: brisk everyday spoken question word (gàn má)

examples.text: 你在这儿干吗？
examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: 你这么着急跑过来干吗？
examples.trans: Why did you come running over in such a hurry?

meanings.note: Pinyin: píng píng. Reduplication of 平 ('flat/even/smooth'), often followed by 的 after resultative 得 (熨得平平的 'ironed nice and flat').

examples.text: 小晴把四块白亚麻桌布都熨得平平的，没有一道褶子。
examples.trans: Qing ironed all four white linen tablecloths nice and flat without a single crease.

examples.text: 刚铺好的石板路平平的，推着小餐车走非常稳。
examples.trans: The newly laid flagstone path is nice and flat, making it very steady to roll a serving cart along.

meanings.note: Noun dǐ (as in 透个底, 'reveal the inside truth').

examples.text: 你就跟我透个底吧，他们谁能赢？
examples.trans: Give me an inside tip — which side is going to win?

examples.text: 充分彩排以后，大家心里都有底了。
examples.trans: After a full rehearsal, everyone felt confident.

张.gloss: measure word for flat surfaces and paper

meanings.en: measure word for flat surfaces and paper
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhāng. Counts tables, beds, paper sheets, tickets, receipts, and luggage tags (一张桌子, 一张纸).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 旁边的把手上系着一张小纸牌。
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied on the side handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Read de after a verb to introduce how it goes (走得快 'walk fast'); read děi before a verb to mean 'must'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: niàn. Used for reading a letter or notice out loud (念第一行 'read the first line aloud').

examples.text: 二十毫米、铜的、热水器阀门——我一路念过去！
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, water-heater valve—I will repeat it all the way!

examples.text: 十九条理由？！您是迎接哥哥，还是念火车时刻表呀？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Pinyin: huāng. Describes feeling rattled or panicked (别慌 'don't panic').

examples.text: 等周经理听说他为分贝慌了一整夜，表情一定精彩！
examples.trans: Wait until Manager Zhou hears he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: 对。我一慌，按了门铃，把星期五纸条贴在把手上。
examples.trans: Yes. In a panic I rang the bell and taped the Friday note onto the handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dài. Specifically for accessories placed on the head, face, neck, or wrist—contrast 穿 for clothes/shoes.

examples.text: 哎呀，怎么拿错了！我戴眼镜看看行李牌。
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and check the luggage tag.

examples.text: 完了！昨天我没戴眼镜，在平板上接了电话预订！
examples.trans: Disaster! Yesterday without my glasses I took a phone booking on the tablet!

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a verb used in conversational Mandarin.

examples.text: 我有一个抄。
examples.trans: I have a 抄.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的抄。
examples.trans: This is a very good 抄.

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a verb used in conversational Mandarin.

examples.text: 我有一个拌。
examples.trans: I have a 拌.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的拌。
examples.trans: This is a very good 拌.

meanings.note: Colloquial predicate pīn ('pushing oneself to the limit').

examples.text: 你太拼了！
examples.trans: You are pushing yourself way too hard!

examples.text: 为了节目大家都很拼。
examples.trans: Everyone goes all-out for the show.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tǐng. As an adverb, 'quite' (挺好); as a verb, 'straighten up' (挺起) or 'pull through' (挺过).

examples.text: 你看，早餐忙乱和神秘电话你都挺过来了！
examples.trans: Look, you made it through both the breakfast rush and the mystery phone call!

examples.text: 挺起肩膀，志豪先生。记住那三句简单的话——我去开门！
examples.trans: Shoulders back, Mr Zhihao. Remember those three simple lines—I will open the gate!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tuī. Opposite of 拉 ('pull'); used for pushing doors open.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 这扇木门往里推就开了。
examples.trans: Push this wooden door inward and it opens.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a verb used in conversational Mandarin.

examples.text: 我有一个撕破。
examples.trans: I have a 撕破.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的撕破。
examples.trans: This is a very good 撕破.

meanings.note: Verb/noun zhīchí ('back up, support').

examples.text: 如果没有各位的支持，也不会合作得这么好。
examples.trans: Without everyone's support, cooperation would not go so well.

examples.text: 谢谢观众朋友们一直以来的支持。
examples.trans: Thank you to our viewers for your steady support.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhěng. Combines with a measure word to mean 'the entire' (整条街 'the whole street', 整栋楼 'the whole building').

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 今晚半价，而且一整周早餐免费！
examples.trans: Half price tonight, plus free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Pinyin: páng biān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 旁边位置 ('a spot beside').

examples.text: 旁边的把手上系着一张小纸牌。
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied on the side handle.

examples.text: 看拉链旁边……对，有她的名字缩写！
examples.trans: Check beside the zipper... yes, her name initials are here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí jiān jiāo náng. Compound 时间 ('time') + 胶囊 ('capsule'); measure word: 个 (gè).

examples.text: 出远门回家以前，我和您姑姑藏了一个小铁盒时间胶囊。
examples.trans: Before my long journey home, your aunt and I hid a small tin time capsule.

examples.text: 时间胶囊里装着三十年前的手绘地图和一张旧照片。
examples.trans: Inside the time capsule were a thirty-year-old hand-drawn map and an old photograph.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī liù. Literally 'week-day six'; Mainland standard alongside informal 周六 (zhōu liù).

examples.text: 每个星期六早上，这条老街都有热闹的集市。
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning, this old street hosts a lively market.

examples.text: 星期六下午来院子里喝杯热柠檬茶吧。
examples.trans: Come to the courtyard for a cup of hot lemon tea on Saturday afternoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个星期天 ('a Sunday').

examples.text: 从那天起我们就再没说过话。上周我给他寄了一张明信片。
examples.trans: Since that day we have not spoken again. Last week I mailed him a postcard.

examples.text: 星期天早上大家都不急着赶车，慢慢喝早茶。
examples.trans: On Sunday mornings nobody rushes for trains, lingering over tea instead.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì hòu. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最后一个 ('the last one').

examples.text: 上楼梯，平台往左拐，最上面最后一扇门。
examples.trans: Up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the very top.

examples.text: 冬天用掉最后一个了。只有桥那边的老五金店有这个尺寸。
examples.trans: Used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǒu. Expresses both possession ('I have') and existence ('there is'); ALWAYS negated with 没 (没有), never 不.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xìng rén. Combines 杏 ('apricot/almond') + 仁 ('nut kernel').

examples.text: 小美端来了一盘刚出炉的温热杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Mei brought over a plate of warm almond biscuits fresh from the oven.

examples.text: 用杏仁粉做的柠檬挞底吃起来特别香酥。
examples.trans: A lemon tart crust made with ground almonds tastes wonderfully crisp and nutty.

meanings.note: Documents/data prepared for review, or physical materials.

examples.text: 她整理好全套演员资料和舆情材料送去演播室。
examples.trans: She compiled the full actor profile and sentiment materials for the studio.

examples.text: 申请立项之前请把所有预算材料准备齐全。
examples.trans: Please prepare all budget materials before filing for greenlight.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lái. Movement toward the speaker, as main verb or directional complement (进来 'come in').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhī. Classifier for slender plant stems, flower sprays, or herb sprigs (两小枝香草 'two small sprigs of herbs', 一枝玫瑰 'a rose stem').

examples.text: 小美让志鹏用细棉绳绑好两小枝刚摘下来的新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Mei had Peng tie two small sprigs of freshly picked herbs together with fine cotton string.

examples.text: 小晴在玻璃花瓶里插了一枝嫩绿的枝叶，桌子一下子亮了起来。
examples.trans: Qing placed a sprig of fresh green foliage in the glass vase, brightening the table right up.

meanings.en: just right; happen to; right on the dot
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng hǎo. Marks a lucky coincidence or exact fit.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

examples.text: 他拿旧阀门比对了——架子上正好还剩两个！
examples.trans: He matched it against the old valve—he has two left on the shelf!

meanings.note: Pinyin: měi. Usually followed by a measure word (每个星期 'every week', 每位客人 'every guest').

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuǐ hén. Combines 水 ('water') + 痕 ('mark/trace/streak').

examples.text: 温水里加一滴白醋，擦完的老玻璃一点水痕都不留。
examples.trans: Add one drop of vinegar to warm water and the wiped old glass leaves zero water streaks.

examples.text: 请用干棉布把木桌上的水痕擦干净。
examples.trans: Please wipe the water marks off the wooden table with a dry cotton cloth.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng qīng chǔ chǔ. AABB reduplication of 清楚 ('clear/distinct'); often used after 看得 or 听得 ('see/hear clearly').

examples.text: 老陈，你在笑呢！我在灯光底下看得清清楚楚！
examples.trans: You are smiling, Chen! I saw it crystal clear under the lamplight!

examples.text: 院子里的每一个人都把小提琴和钢琴的合奏听得清清楚楚。
examples.trans: Everyone in the courtyard heard the violin and piano duet crystal clear.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dī. Used as a verb ('drip') or measure word for drops of liquid.

examples.text: 天哪！桌子上一滴没洒……全洒在我领带上了！
examples.trans: Good heavens! Not a drop spilled on the table... it all spilled on my tie!

examples.text: 老橡木，八十年了，一滴水都不漏。
examples.trans: Old oak, eighty years old—not a single drop leaks.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kǎo. Used for baking bread, rolls, and cakes in an oven.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 多烤几块边角，好姑娘！
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, dear girl!

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhí dào. Combines 直 ('straight') + 到 ('reach/until').

examples.text: 志豪决定留在成都，直到星期五的开幕之夜。
examples.trans: Hao decided to stay in Chengdu right until Friday's opening night.

examples.text: 这场大雨从半夜一直下，直到第二天中午才停。
examples.trans: This heavy rain fell from midnight until noon the next day before stopping.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mī. Action verb for narrowing the eyes into a slit to read small print or smile warmly (眯着眼睛看 'squint to read').

examples.text: 小晴把价钱写得很大很清楚，谁都不用眯着眼睛费力去看。
examples.trans: Qing wrote the prices big and clear so nobody has to squint to read them.

examples.text: 院子里的老猫晒着太阳，舒服得眯起了眼睛。
examples.trans: Basking in the sun in the courtyard, the old cat narrowed its eyes contentedly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǎn. Counts quick looks after verbs of looking (看一眼, 扫一眼 'take a quick look').

examples.text: 太好了……趁着等他们，我扫一眼这封房东来信。
examples.trans: Wonderful... while we wait, let me glance at this letter from the landlord.

examples.text: 小晴，替我念第一行。快说是我眼镜又看花眼了！
examples.trans: Qing, read the top line for me. Tell me my glasses are playing tricks on my eyes!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yán jiū. Works as both verb and noun.

examples.text: 一位研究成都历史小院建筑的建筑师啊！
examples.trans: An architect who studies historic courtyard buildings in Chengdu!

examples.text: 他专门研究南方老城区的木结构建筑。
examples.trans: He specializes in studying timber architecture in historic southern quarters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pò. Describes torn paper, cracked cups, or worn-out items.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

examples.text: 快去跟他聊聊，小晴，不然木地板都要踩破了！
examples.trans: Go talk to him quickly, Qing, or he will wear right through the wooden floorboards!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǒng. Read zhǒng as a measure word for kinds/types (这种, 那种); read zhòng as the verb 'plant/grow'.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

examples.text: 老房子连着旧回忆——那种争吵最伤人。
examples.trans: Old houses are tied to old memories—arguments like that cut deepest.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mì mì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个秘密 ('a secret').

examples.text: 真的吗？我厨房的墙后面真的有一个秘密房间？
examples.trans: Is it true? Is there really a secret room behind my kitchen wall?

examples.text: 这是我们两个人的秘密。
examples.trans: This is a secret between the two of us.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn dān. Everyday adjective for straightforward tasks.

examples.text: 挺起肩膀，志豪先生。记住那三句简单的话——我去开门！
examples.trans: Shoulders back, Mr Zhihao. Remember those three simple lines—I will open the gate!

examples.text: 这道炒蛋做法很简单，味道却极好。
examples.trans: This scrambled-egg recipe is simple, yet tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mǐ sè. Joins 米 ('rice') + 色 ('color'). Refers to the pale yellowish color of unpolished rice.

examples.text: 信封是用厚实的米色纸张做的，摸起来很有质感。
examples.trans: The envelope is made of thick beige paper and feels highly textured.

examples.text: 小美今天穿了一件米色的毛衣，显得特别温柔。
examples.trans: Mei wore a beige sweater today, making her look especially gentle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: táng shuāng. Measure word (量词): 层 (céng), e.g. 一层糖霜 ('a layer of frosting').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 正在架子上放凉呢——金黄外皮配甜柠檬糖霜！
examples.trans: Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust with sweet lemon glaze!

related.gloss: a layer of frosting (measure word 层)

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张纸 ('a sheet of paper').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

related.gloss: a sheet of paper (measure word 张)

meanings.note: Pinyin: láo bǎn. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位老板 ('a boss / shop owner').

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

examples.text: 老板正在开锁呢！别挂电话，等我一秒钟。
examples.trans: The owner is unlocking it right now! Stay on the phone, wait one second.

related.gloss: a boss / shop owner (measure word 位)

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǎo huā jìng. Combines 老花 ('presbyopia / farsightedness of middle age') + 镜 ('glasses/lenses'); measure word: 副 (fù).

examples.text: 周经理摸了摸额头问：“等等——我的老花镜现在是不是又架在额头上？”
examples.trans: Manager Zhou felt his forehead and asked, 'Wait—are my reading glasses perched up on my forehead again right now?'

examples.text: 老陈看细小的钢琴零件时，总会从口袋里拿出那副老花镜戴上。
examples.trans: Whenever Chen inspects tiny piano parts, he takes that pair of reading glasses out of his pocket and puts them on.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huā yuán. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个小花园 ('a small garden').

examples.text: 啊！看这儿：一楼，九号房，花园阳光房！
examples.trans: Aha! Look here: ground floor, Room Nine, garden sunroom!

examples.text: 等等，我们一楼有一个花园阳光房？
examples.trans: Wait, we have a garden sunroom on the ground floor?

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá bēi. Measure word (量词): 只 (zhǐ), e.g. 一只茶杯 ('a teacup').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 里面的茶杯呢？还完好吗？
examples.trans: And the teacup inside? Is it still intact?

meanings.note: Pinyin: méi guǒ. Measure word (量词): 颗 (kē) or 篮 (lán). Joins 莓 ('berry') + 果 ('fruit').

examples.text: 小美在蛋糕顶上点缀了几颗新鲜的红莓果。
examples.trans: Mei garnished the top of the cake with a few fresh red berries.

examples.text: 这罐果酱是用后院刚摘的野莓果熬制的。
examples.trans: This jar of jam was simmered from wild berries just picked in the backyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cài pǔ. Measure word (量词): 份 (fèn) or 本 (běn). Joins 菜 ('dish, vegetable') + 谱 ('register, manual').

examples.text: 这张泛黄的纸原来是半份祖传的蛋糕菜谱。
examples.trans: This yellowed paper turned out to be half of an ancestral cake recipe.

examples.text: 周经理正坐在前台翻看附近新开饭店的菜谱。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou is sitting at the front desk flipping through the menu of a newly opened restaurant nearby.

meanings.note: Pinyin: luò. Used both literally for raindrops/leaves falling and musically for a phrase landing on a note (落在中央瑞音上).

examples.text: 到了第二十八小节，整段旋律稳稳落在了中央瑞音上。
examples.trans: In bar twenty-eight, the whole melody lands squarely on middle D.

examples.text: 几片金黄的梧桐叶轻轻落在院子的石桌上。
examples.trans: Several golden plane-tree leaves drifted gently down onto the courtyard stone table.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lán. Describes blue suitcases, doors, or teacups.

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

examples.text: 储藏室里有两个软枕头和一块蓝地毯！
examples.trans: In the storeroom there are two soft pillows and a blue rug!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bò he. Measure word (量词): 片 (piàn) or 把 (bǎ). Note the special pronunciation bò he for this specific plant name.

examples.text: 茶杯里飘出淡淡的薄荷清香。
examples.trans: A faint, refreshing mint fragrance wafted from the teacup.

examples.text: 小晴摘下几片薄荷叶，洗干净后放进了冰水里。
examples.trans: Qing picked a few mint leaves, washed them clean, and dropped them into the ice water.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dàn gāo. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块蛋糕 ('a piece of cake').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 十一点二十分。小美，蛋糕好了吗？
examples.trans: Eleven twenty. Mei, is the cake ready?

related.gloss: a piece of cake (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xíng. Read xíng when meaning 'that works / okay' (不行 'won't work'); read háng when counting lines of text (第一行).

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 小晴，替我念第一行。快说是我眼镜又看花眼了！
examples.trans: Qing, read the top line for me. Tell me my glasses are playing tricks on my eyes!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ràng. Everyday causative/polite-offer verb (让我看看 'let me have a look').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 宋老师，让我来给您倒新鲜橙汁！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, allow me to pour fresh orange juice for you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Often reduplicated softly as 试试 ('give it a try').

examples.text: 摸摸热水管——下面是温的，上面变凉了。
examples.trans: Feel the hot-water pipe—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: 这件羊毛开衫很暖和，您试试吧。
examples.trans: This wool cardigan is very warm—try it on.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qǐ lái. Marks standing up or beginning/evaluating an action.

examples.text: 摸摸铜管！已经热起来了！
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: 快把那张纸折起来，塞进口袋里。
examples.trans: Fold up that sheet of paper right now and tuck it into your pocket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chèn. Introduces a favorable moment before it passes (趁热吃 'eat while it's hot').

examples.text: 趁着阳光亮，我能再看看那张小纸牌吗？
examples.trans: While the sunlight is bright, may I look at that small paper tag again?

examples.text: 太好了……趁着等他们，我扫一眼这封房东来信。
examples.trans: Wonderful... while we wait, let me glance at this letter from the landlord.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng qīng. Reduplication of 轻 ('light/soft'), used directly before short verbs or with 地 (轻轻地抽出来).

examples.text: 宋老师用两根手指把旧乐谱轻轻抽了出来。
examples.trans: Teacher Song gently slid the old music sheet out with two fingers.

examples.text: 怕吵醒午睡的客人，小晴轻轻关上了木门。
examples.trans: So as not to wake guests napping at noon, Qing closed the wooden door softly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: biān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一边 ('one side').

examples.text: 对，过了桥，右手边会经过一家绿药店。
examples.trans: Right, after crossing the bridge, you pass a green pharmacy on your right.

examples.text: 快坐在向阳窗户边，宋老师！先别急着上楼！
examples.trans: Sit right down by the sunny window, Teacher Song! No rush to go back upstairs yet!

meanings.note: Pinyin: biān jiǎo. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块边角 ('a corner piece').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 多烤几块边角，好姑娘！
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, dear girl!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jìn. Movement into an enclosed space (请进 'come in!', 倒进 'pour into').

examples.text: 小晴，把热水倒进茶壶里，他们来了！
examples.trans: Qing, pour the hot water into the teapot—here they come!

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lián. Pairs with 都/也 to highlight 'even X' (连名字都一样), or means 'connect' as a verb.

examples.text: 老房子连着旧回忆——那种争吵最伤人。
examples.trans: Old houses are tied to old memories—arguments like that cut deepest.

examples.text: 笔挺又干净，周经理！连眼镜都戴在鼻子上，没在额头上。
examples.trans: Crisp and spotless, Manager Zhou! Even your glasses are on your nose instead of your forehead.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn huáng. Praises freshly baked pastry crusts.

examples.text: 正在架子上放凉呢——金黄外皮配甜柠檬糖霜！
examples.trans: Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust with sweet lemon glaze!

examples.text: 刚烤出来的面包卷外皮一片金黄。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls came out golden-brown.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jí shì. Traditional open-air neighbourhood or farmers' market (星期六集市 'Saturday market').

examples.text: 星期六一早，小晴和小美提着竹篮去逛集市。
examples.trans: First thing Saturday morning, Qing and Mei carry bamboo baskets to browse the street market.

examples.text: 集市上的本地蜂蜜和黄柠檬比超市新鲜多了。
examples.trans: Local honey and yellow lemons at the street market are much fresher than in supermarkets.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǔ diǎn. Combines 雨 ('rain') + 点 ('drop/dot').

examples.text: 快去拿灯笼，第一波大雨点已经掉下来了！
examples.trans: Grab the lantern quickly—the first big raindrops are already falling!

examples.text: 大颗的雨点敲在芭蕉叶上，发出清脆的声响。
examples.trans: Big raindrops pattered crisply onto the banana leaves.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a noun used in conversational Mandarin. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个面糊 ('a 面糊').

examples.text: 我有一个面糊。
examples.trans: I have a 面糊.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的面糊。
examples.trans: This is a very good 面糊.

颗.gloss: measure word for small round things

meanings.en: measure word for small round things
meanings.note: Pinyin: kē. Counts stars, pearls, beans, buttons, and hearts (一颗星 'a star').

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

examples.text: 小盘子里放着五颗新鲜草莓。
examples.trans: Five fresh strawberries sit on the small plate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng cǎo. Measure word (量词): 盆, e.g. 一盆香草 ('a pot of herbs').

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

related.gloss: a pot of herbs (measure word 盆)
